structure: Part 3, Reading, listing, deleting and expiry. Read in full: NotificationController (266 lines) and NotificationService (548 lines), claiming only GET /notifications, GET /notifications/{ref}/fulfilments, GET /notifications/reference-numbers, POST /notifications/{ref}/soft-delete, DELETE /notifications and deleteExpired; NotificationRepository, NotificationSort, NotificationView and NotificationViewData (list item shape), NotificationFulfilmentsView, NotificationReferenceOnly, NotificationPageResponse (1-based paging), ReferenceNumberPageResponse (0-based paging), NotificationExpirySweeper, NotificationTtlConfig, AdminSecretFilter, and the admin.secret and notification.admin, notification.list and notification.ttl sections of application.yml. Tests read in full: NotificationControllerTest (1395 lines; the FindAll, FindFulfilments, FindAllReferenceNumbers, SoftDelete, Delete and replay-401 tests are claimed as proof, the create/replace/copy/submit/amend/cancel-amend/outbox-events tests belong to other parts), NotificationSortTest, NotificationExpirySweeperTest, NotificationExpirySweeperConditionTest, NotificationTtlConfigTest and NotificationExpiryIT. Covered: dashboard list scoping (none: status-filtered only), paging and fixed page size 25, the four sort options and fallback, the exact referenceNumber filter, list item fields; the fulfilment read; the reference-number list (admin page size 50, newest first); soft delete statuses, idempotency, refusals and events; hard DELETE all-or-nothing with audit; the admin-secret guard; draft expiry stamping, prod safeguards, sweep cadence, batch, lock and cascade. Claims 001-076 restate the earlier run of this part, re-verified against the source; 077-093 add test proofs and details that run missed.

claims.statement: GET /notifications returns a paginated list of import notifications for the dashboard.
claims.quote:
@Operation(summary = "List notifications",
        description = "Returns a paginated list of import notifications. "

claims.statement: The dashboard list only ever includes notifications in DRAFT, SUBMITTED or AMEND status; soft-deleted (DELETED) notifications never appear in it.
claims.quote:
List<NotificationStatus> dashboardStatuses = List.of(
            NotificationStatus.DRAFT, NotificationStatus.SUBMITTED, NotificationStatus.AMEND);

claims.statement: The dashboard list is not scoped to the calling user or organisation: the endpoint takes no user or organisation input, so every caller is served notifications from every trader. This is a weakness in access control on the list read.
claims.note: Inferred from the absence of any user, organisation or actor parameter on the list endpoint and its repository query (findAllViewByStatusIn filters on status only). Stated in general terms on purpose.

claims.statement: The dashboard list's page parameter is 1-based, defaults to 1 and must be at least 1.
claims.note: The response status for page=0 is set by GlobalExceptionHandler, which another part reads.

claims.statement: The dashboard list returns 25 notifications per page, set by configuration; the caller cannot choose the page size.
The dashboard list supports four sort options: arrivalDate,desc (the default), arrivalDate,asc, createdAt,desc and createdAt,asc.
claims.quote: Optional sort: arrivalDate,desc (default), arrivalDate,asc, createdAt,desc, createdAt,asc.

claims.statement: Sorting by arrivalDate orders on the transport arrival date of the notification, and sorting by createdAt orders on when the notification was created.
claims.quote:
private static final String ARRIVAL_DATE_FIELD = "notification.transport.arrivalDate";
    private static final String CREATED_AT_FIELD = "created";

claims.statement: A missing, blank, malformed (not exactly field,direction) or unknown sort value falls back to arrival date, newest first, rather than being rejected.
claims.note: NotificationSortTest.toSort_shouldDefaultToArrivalDateDescending_whenMissingOrInvalid proves null, empty and "invalid" all give arrival date descending.

claims.statement: The sort direction is ascending only when the direction part is "asc" (any case); any other direction value sorts descending.
The dashboard list can be filtered by an optional referenceNumber, which is an exact match against a complete notification reference, not a partial search.
claims.quote: Optional referenceNumber: exact match against a complete notification reference.

claims.statement: The referenceNumber filter is trimmed of surrounding whitespace, and a blank value is treated as no filter.
A reference filter that matches nothing (including a reference that does not exist, is soft-deleted, or is not in a valid reference format) returns 200 with an empty page, not an error.
claims.note: findAll_shouldPassInvalidReferenceNumberToService proves the controller passes "invalid-ref" through and answers 200; the reference filter is not pattern-validated.

claims.statement: The dashboard list offers no other filter or search: only page, sort and an exact referenceNumber are accepted, so there is no filter by status, date, commodity, country or free text.
claims.note: Inferred from the three request parameters being the endpoint's entire input.

claims.statement: The dashboard list response carries content, page (1-based, echoing the request), size, numberOfElements, totalElements and totalPages.
claims.quote:
public record NotificationPageResponse(
    List<NotificationView> content,
    int page,
    int size,
    int numberOfElements,
    long totalElements,
    int totalPages)
claims.note: page is the zero-based page number plus 1 (pageResult.getNumber() + 1). NotificationControllerTest.findAll_shouldReturnEmptyPage pins an empty page as page 1, size 25 and zero totals.

claims.statement: Each dashboard list item carries the notification's referenceNumber, concurrencyToken, status, created timestamp, origin, commodity, consignor, consignee and transport, as a flat object.
claims.note: The other accessors are getCommodity, getConsignor, getConsignee and getTransport, each unwrapped from notification.*.

claims.statement: List items do not carry submittedAt, the updated timestamp, importer, destination, reason for import or the fulfilments payload, so a dashboard built on this endpoint cannot show those.
claims.note: Inferred from the projection's accessor list, which the response serialises directly (NotificationPageResponse javadoc: the wire response carries exactly the fields the projection exposes).

claims.statement: The created timestamp on list items is an ISO-8601 instant in UTC with a Z suffix and sub-second precision, not a date or a numeric epoch.
The dashboard list endpoint loads the whole stored notification for every row, a cost accepted because the endpoint is due to be replaced by an event-populated dashboard service.
claims.quote:
Accepted trade-off: this endpoint is being replaced by an event-populated dashboard service
 * and there are no live users to notice the cost.

claims.statement: GET /notifications/{referenceNumber}/fulfilments returns the notification's referenceNumber, concurrencyToken, status, created, submittedAt and its opaque fulfilments payload; it backs the frontend engine's rehydrate of a journey.
claims.quote: Returns the fulfilment-view projection (referenceNumber, status, dates, opaque fulfilments payload) of the notification at the given reference. Backs the frontend engine's rehydrate path.

claims.statement: The fulfilment read leaves out the server-only fields: the pre-amend notification and fulfilment snapshots and the expiry time.
claims.quote:
Server-only fields
 * ({@code preAmendNotification}, {@code preAmendFulfilments}, {@code expireAt}) are
 * intentionally omitted so they aren't loaded on read.

claims.statement: The fulfilment read returns created and submittedAt as exact ISO-8601 UTC instants with a Z suffix.
Reading the fulfilments of a reference that does not exist returns 404 with the detail "Cannot find notification with reference number: <reference>".
The fulfilment read returns a notification in any status, including a soft-deleted one.
claims.note: Inferred: the lookup is by reference alone, with no status condition, unlike the dashboard list.

claims.statement: The fulfilment read is not scoped to the caller: any caller who knows a reference number is served that notification's content. This is a weakness in access control on the read.
claims.note: Inferred from the endpoint taking only the reference and the admin-secret filter not covering it. Stated in general terms on purpose.

claims.statement: The fulfilment read and soft delete only accept a path reference in the GBN-AG format: GBN-AG-, a two-digit year, a hyphen and six characters from digits and capital letters excluding I, L, O and U.
claims.note: The response a malformed reference gets comes from GlobalExceptionHandler, read by another part.

claims.statement: GET /notifications/reference-numbers returns a paginated list of notification reference numbers only, without the notifications' content.
claims.quote: Returns a paginated list of notification reference numbers without loading full documents

claims.statement: The reference-number list's page parameter is 0-based, defaults to 0 and must be at least 0, and the page it reports is 0-based too, unlike the dashboard list, which is 1-based.
claims.note: NotificationControllerTest.findAllReferenceNumbers_shouldReturnEmptyPage pins page 0 for the default request.

claims.statement: The reference-number list returns 50 references per page, set by the admin page-size configuration.
The reference-number list is ordered by creation time, newest first.
The reference-number list includes every stored notification in any status, soft-deleted ones included.
claims.note: Inferred: the query has no status condition.

claims.statement: The reference-number list response carries content (a list of reference strings), page, size, numberOfElements, totalElements and totalPages.
claims.quote:
public record ReferenceNumberPageResponse(
    List<String> content,
    int page,
    int size,
    int numberOfElements,
    long totalElements,
    int totalPages)

claims.statement: The reference-number list documents a 401 Unauthorised response but is not behind the admin secret or any other check, so any caller can list every reference. This is a weakness in access control.
claims.note: Inferred: the admin-secret filter skips every GET request. Stated in general terms on purpose.

claims.statement: POST /notifications/{referenceNumber}/soft-delete moves the notification to DELETED status and returns the updated notification with 200.
claims.quote: Transitions notification status to DELETED (soft delete).

claims.statement: Soft delete accepts a notification in DRAFT, SUBMITTED or AMEND status.
The soft-delete API description says only DRAFT and SUBMITTED notifications can be deleted, which disagrees with the code, which also deletes AMEND notifications.
claims.quote: Only DRAFT and SUBMITTED notifications can be deleted.
claims.note: Recorded as a discrepancy inside this source: the published OpenAPI text lags NotificationService.softDeleteNotification.

claims.statement: Soft-deleting a notification that is already DELETED is a no-op that returns the notification unchanged with 200, so a repeated request after a lost response is safe.
Soft delete refuses any other status with 400 and the detail "Cannot delete notification with status: <status>"; with today's four statuses this refusal cannot be reached.
claims.note: Unreachable is inferred: NotificationStatus is DRAFT, SUBMITTED, AMEND, DELETED, and DELETED returns early. NotificationControllerTest.softDelete_shouldReturn400_whenNotificationNotInDeletableState mocks the service to throw this message for DELETED, which the real service no longer does.

claims.statement: Soft-deleting a reference that does not exist returns 404 with the detail "Cannot find notification with reference number: <reference>".
Soft delete keeps the notification record and its content; only its status changes to DELETED and its updated time is refreshed.
claims.note: Inferred from writeWithOutbox saving the same aggregate with only status and updated changed. A soft delete from AMEND keeps the pre-amend snapshots and submittedAt, because NOTIFICATION_SUBMISSION_DELETED is not one of the SUBMISSION_EVENTS that clear them.

claims.statement: Soft-deleting a DRAFT records a NotificationDeleted event; soft-deleting a SUBMITTED or AMEND notification records a NotificationSubmissionDeleted event, for publishing to other services.
Soft delete takes an optional actor body (id, source, userType, displayName, organisationId) and an optional x-cdp-request-id header, which it passes on as the event's actor and correlation id.
claims.quote:
@RequestHeader(value = HEADER_TRACE_ID, required = false, defaultValue = "") String traceId,
        @RequestBody(required = false) ActorRequest actorRequest)

claims.statement: Soft delete has no ownership or admin check: the endpoint is not behind the admin secret and does not compare the caller with the notification's owner. This is a weakness in access control.
claims.note: Inferred: the admin filter covers only DELETE requests and the replay POST, and the service makes no caller check. The documented 401 is never produced. Stated in general terms on purpose.

claims.statement: DELETE /notifications permanently removes the notifications named in a JSON array of reference numbers, together with their accompanying documents, and answers 204 No Content.
DELETE /notifications with an empty list is refused with 400 and nothing is deleted.
DELETE /notifications requires both an x-cdp-request-id header and a User-Id header; a request missing either is refused with 400 before anything is deleted.
claims.quote:
@RequestHeader(value = NotificationController.HEADER_TRACE_ID, required = true) String traceId,
        @RequestHeader(value = NotificationController.HEADER_USER_ID, required = true) String userId)

claims.statement: DELETE /notifications is all or nothing: if any listed reference does not exist, nothing is deleted and the caller gets 404 with the detail "Cannot find notifications with reference numbers: <missing references, comma-separated>".
claims.quote:
throw new NotFoundException(
                "Cannot find notifications with reference numbers: " + String.join(", ", missing));

claims.statement: DELETE /notifications deletes notifications in any status: it has no status check.
claims.quote: public void deleteByReferenceNumbers(List<String> referenceNumbers, AuditContext auditContext) {
claims.note: Inferred from the method checking existence only.

claims.statement: Every DELETE /notifications request writes an audit record of action DELETE_NOTIFICATIONS with the result (SUCCESS, or FAILURE when a reference is missing), the references, their count, the trace id, the user id and a timestamp; the FAILURE record is kept even though the request fails.
claims.note: The FAILURE record survives because the method is @Transactional(noRollbackFor = NotFoundException.class).

claims.statement: DELETE /notifications records no lifecycle event, so other services are not told that the notifications were removed.
claims.note: Inferred: neither deleteByReferenceNumbers nor deleteNotificationsAndDocuments calls the outbox service, unlike soft delete.

claims.statement: DELETE requests to /notifications and POST requests to /notifications/{reference}/replay require the Trade-Imports-Animals-Admin-Secret header to match the configured admin secret.
claims.note: The class javadoc says "Applied to DELETE /notifications requests only.", which predates the replay guard. The DELETE match is a prefix match, so any DELETE under /notifications is guarded too.

claims.statement: A guarded request with no admin secret header, or the wrong one, gets 401 with an empty body and never reaches the endpoint.
When the configured admin secret is blank, every guarded request is refused with 401.
The admin secret is compared in constant time.
The admin secret is set from the TRADE_IMPORTS_ANIMALS_ADMIN_SECRET environment variable, with a local default when it is not set.
claims.note: Default value redacted. A deployed environment that does not set the variable would fall back to that default.

claims.statement: Every GET endpoint and every POST other than replay, including soft delete and the reference-number list, is outside the admin-secret guard.
In non-prod environments, each newly created notification is stamped to expire a configured number of days after its creation time.
The expiry window is set by the NOTIFICATION_TTL_DAYS environment variable and is unset by default, so by default no notification expires.
claims.quote:
# Defaults here are the prod-safe values: days unset (no stamping) and sweep disabled.
  # Non-prod environments opt in via NOTIFICATION_TTL_DAYS and NOTIFICATION_TTL_SWEEP_ENABLED.
  ttl:
    days: ${NOTIFICATION_TTL_DAYS:}
claims.note: The code comments describe the window as 7 days ("suit 7-day granularity"), but 7 is not configured in this repo; the value comes from each environment's config.

claims.statement: No expiry is stamped when the running environment is prod (the ENVIRONMENT value "prod" in any case), even if a number of days is configured; any other name, including "production", counts as non-prod.
Expiry is anchored to creation: saving, submitting or amending a notification does not extend its expiry.
claims.quote:
Anchored to {@code created}, so a notification expires a fixed window after creation
     * regardless of later activity.

claims.statement: Expiry is not limited to drafts: a notification of any status, submitted ones included, is deleted once its expiry time passes.
claims.note: Inferred: the expiry query has no status condition, and stamping happens for every created notification. The partition scope calls it "draft expiry"; the code does not restrict it to drafts.

claims.statement: A copied notification gets its own expiry window counted from the copy's creation time.
claims.note: Inferred: copy goes through createNotification, which calls stampExpiry.

claims.statement: A notification with no expiry time, such as one created before expiry shipped or in prod, is never deleted by the sweep.
claims.quote:
Notifications with a {@code null} {@code expireAt}
     * — including everything created before this feature shipped — are never selected.

claims.statement: A notification is due for deletion once its expiry time is at or before the time of the sweep.
claims.quote: Notifications due for automatic expiry: a non-null {@code expireAt} at or before {@code now}.

claims.statement: The expiry sweep runs only where notification.ttl.sweep.enabled is explicitly true (NOTIFICATION_TTL_SWEEP_ENABLED); it is off by default and absent when the setting is false or missing.
Prod is protected from expiry by two independent safeguards: no expiry is stamped there, and the sweep does not run there.
claims.quote:
Prod is protected by two independent safeguards. Deleting a notification in prod would require
 * both to fail together:

claims.statement: The expiry sweep runs once an hour by default, measured from the end of the previous run.
Each sweep deletes at most 10 expired notifications by default; any more wait for the next run.
claims.note: NotificationExpiryIT.deleteExpired_removesAtMostBatchSizePerRun proves three due notifications with batch 2 are removed as 2 then 1.

claims.statement: The expiry sweep permanently deletes each due notification together with its accompanying documents.
claims.quote:
Deletes notifications whose {@code expireAt} has passed, cascading to their accompanying
     * documents, up to {@code batchSize} per call.

claims.statement: The expiry sweep writes no audit record, and leaves existing audit records that name the expired notification untouched.
claims.quote:
unlike {@link #deleteByReferenceNumbers} it writes no audit
     * record

claims.statement: The expiry sweep records no lifecycle event, so other services are not told that an expired notification was removed.
claims.note: Inferred: deleteExpired never calls the outbox service.

claims.statement: The expiry sweep tolerates documents disappearing mid-batch rather than failing, because another actor may remove them at the same time.
claims.quote:
tolerates documents vanishing mid-batch (a background sweep should not fail because
     * another actor removed a row concurrently)

claims.statement: Only one service instance sweeps at a time: each run takes a shared lock named notification-expiry-sweeper, held at least 1 second and at most 30 seconds, and skips the run if the lock is held elsewhere.
When a sweep deletes notifications it logs "Expiry sweeper deleted <n> notification(s)"; a sweep that deletes nothing logs nothing.
A configured expiry window of zero or a negative number of days fails validation when the service starts, rather than stamping an expiry that has already passed.
Sweep settings that are zero, negative or missing fall back to safe defaults: batch size 10, interval 1 hour, lock held at least 1 second and at most 30 seconds.

The backend offers no read of a single notification's full content by reference other than the fulfilment view; a dashboard or check-answers page reading the stored notification fields has only the list item fields or the opaque fulfilments payload to use.
claims.note: Looked at every GET mapping in NotificationController: /notifications, /{referenceNumber}/fulfilments, /reference-numbers and /{referenceNumber}/outbox-events. None returns the full notification aggregate by reference.

claims.statement: A test proves that GET /notifications with nothing stored answers 200 with an empty content array, page 1, size 25 and zero numberOfElements, totalElements and totalPages.
claims.note: WebMvc slice test with the service mocked: it proves the wire shape and status, not the query.

claims.statement: A test proves that each GET /notifications list item is serialised with its referenceNumber, status, origin country code and commodity name, and that the page, size, totalElements and totalPages are returned alongside.
Tests prove that the page, sort and referenceNumber query parameters of GET /notifications reach the list unchanged, including a referenceNumber that is not in a valid reference format.
When the dashboard list is filtered by a reference that matches, the response holds exactly that one notification and reports a total of one.
Tests prove that GET /notifications/reference-numbers answers 200 with a list of reference strings and a 0-based page, and that a requested page number is passed through.
claims.note: The tests' mocked size of 25 is fixture data; the configured admin page size is 50 (repo-backend-p3-028).

claims.statement: A test proves that DELETE /notifications with the admin secret, a trace id and a user id answers 204 and passes the trace id and user id on for the audit record.

The soft-delete controller test pins a 400 refusal with the detail "Cannot delete notification with status: DELETED", but the service treats a repeat soft delete of a DELETED notification as a successful no-op, so that refusal is never produced for DELETED in practice.
claims.quote: .thenThrow(new BadRequestException("Cannot delete notification with status: DELETED"));
claims.note: The test mocks the service, so it proves only that a BadRequestException maps to 400 with its message as detail. The real service returns early for DELETED (repo-backend-p3-036).

claims.statement: The admin-secret guard applies to any DELETE request whose path begins with /notifications, not only to DELETE /notifications itself.
claims.note: The class comment says 'Applied to DELETE /notifications requests only.', which is narrower than the code and omits the replay endpoint the code also guards.

claims.statement: The admin-secret check runs before almost every other request filter, so a refused request is turned away before any other request handling.
claims.note: Inferred from the filter's order, one step after the highest precedence.

claims.statement: Tests prove the admin-secret guard and the DELETE /notifications headers are checked with the secret supplied as the Trade-Imports-Animals-Admin-Secret header; every DELETE test sends it.
claims.note: The test value is a test fixture, not a real secret. No test in this file sends DELETE /notifications without the secret; the 401 path is proven only for replay (repo-backend-p3-051).

claims.statement: A test proves that the expiry sweep leaves a notification that is not yet due, and its accompanying document, in place.
claims.quote:
// Non-due notification and its document survive.
        assertThat(notificationRepository.findByReferenceNumber(activeRef)).isPresent();

claims.statement: When the expiry sweep finds notifications due, it logs "Expiring <n> notification(s)" before deleting them.
Each expiry sweep batch deletes its notifications and their documents in one transaction.
The environment name used to decide whether expiry is stamped comes from the ENVIRONMENT variable and is "local" when that is not set.
The interval between expiry sweeps can be set by notification.ttl.sweep.interval-ms, and falls back to one hour (3600000 ms) when it is not set.
No test in this slice proves the status filter or the sort order of GET /notifications against a real store: the list tests mock the service, and only the sort parsing is unit-tested.
claims.note: Looked in NotificationControllerTest, NotificationSortTest and NotificationExpiryIT, the tests this part reads. Other integration tests outside this part may cover it.

claims.statement: A path reference on the fulfilment read or soft delete that is not in the GBN-AG format is refused by request validation before any lookup; the status and message of that refusal are set by the shared error handler, not in this slice.
claims.note: Inferred from @Validated on the controller and @Pattern on the path variable. GlobalExceptionHandler handles ConstraintViolationException; it is read by another part.
